html:
SMTO-GWT-0032 — A computer refused one step of a file copy

GUID: e0bbd125-4c35-49f8-bf53-83ec3cc2d937
Slug: gateway-transfer-rejected
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • While SMTO was copying a file between two computers, the Gateway on one of them refused a step, so SMTO stopped the copy. Earlier steps may already have written part of the file at the destination.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, expand each computer involved in the copy, and under Software updates select Check for updates. Install any update offered. A Gateway that is older than SMTO often refuses copy steps it does not understand.
  2. On the receiving computer, look in the destination folder for a partial or finished copy of the file. Steps before the refused one may already have created or changed that file.
  3. Once both computers are up to date, ask SMTO in a new message to copy the file again, saying whether it may replace what is already there. A new copy starts cleanly, and telling SMTO about the existing file avoids replacing something you want to keep.

What success looks like

  • The copy finishes and the Task reports the file at its destination with the expected size.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateways, saying which two computers were involved. Update Gateways only through Check for updates; don't copy Gateway program files over by hand.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway rejected a transfer operation (a documented 400/404/405/422/501 rejection from /transfer/operation, or a non-ok transfer receipt without a usable error kind), so the copy stopped as transfer_rejected; the receipt may mark the step's effect as unknown.

What this means

  • The transfer path rejected a documented protocol status, detected an oversized or mismatched receipt, or received a negative transfer result. These conditions have different execution certainty. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The transfer path rejected a documented protocol status, detected an oversized or mismatched receipt, or received a negative transfer result. These conditions have different execution certainty.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the rejection status, transfer ID, receipt bounds and retained effect-unknown flag; separate admission rejection from an invalid post-dispatch receipt.

How to fix it

  • Read the rejection status, transfer ID and effect_unknown flag in Technical details or the Server log. A 404/405/501 on /transfer/operation usually means that Gateway is older than the Server's transfer protocol, so update it through the supported Gateway update path; for 400/422, compare Server and Gateway versions. Then inspect the destination path before starting a new copy, which gets a new transfer ID.
  • Correct a proven rejected request or protocol mismatch. For invalid or lost receipts, inspect the original transfer and destination before another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The protocol defect is resolved and any potentially completed transfer step is reconciled under its original identity.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
